own_scenes.desc: El funk abre la puerta a la subcultura disco: los gays de Nueva York, perseguidos, crean sus islas sociales en clubes privados y recuperan la despersonalización del éxtasis colectivo. Tres hechos la impulsan: el soul orquestal de Barry White, «Autobahn» de Kraftwerk y el Polymoog. Manu Dibango («Soul Makossa») y MFSB la inventan; Giorgio Moroder casa la música robótica de Kraftwerk con el soul (Donna Summer, «I Feel Love», nacimiento del synth-pop). Van McCoy, el maxi de 12" de Walter Gibbons, Chic, Grace Jones, Gloria Gaynor, Saturday Night Fever, el Warehouse de Frankie Knuckles y el Paradise Garage de Larry Levan. Los reyes del pop: Michael Jackson (Thriller, «el mayor farol de todos los tiempos») y Prince, su contrapartida intelectual.

podcast.title: Beginning of the End (1978)
podcast.body: Professionally, the beginning of the end for disco music is marked in 1978 with Gloria Gaynor's release of "I Will Survive," which is considered the last great quality disco hit. After this point, disco began to degenerate into a form that was almost self-parody, becoming somewhat scatological, parodic, and sometimes ridiculous. "el principio del final de la música disco es en 1978 cuando Gloria Gaynor publica el I will Survive."

podcast.title: 1990s Resurgence
podcast.body: In the 1990s, thanks to the Pechos Boys' pivotal 1993 album "Very" and their consistent work throughout the 1980s, disco influences saw an enormous resurgence and reinterpretation. This impact was evident in the careers of artists like Madonna (culminating in "Confessions on a Dancefloor"), U2 (in songs like "Lemon"), Kylie Minogue, and Jamiroquai. "en los 90 gracias a los Pechos Boys esas influencias de la música disco que tanto habían estado defendido y evolucionando los Pechos Boys durante los 80 a partir de ese disco en el 93 pues explotan."

podcast.title: Defining Decade (1970s)
podcast.body: Disco music unequivocally defined the 1970s, characterizing the music of that decade in both its dance club and more pop-oriented forms. It emerged rapidly and appeared to die just as quickly. "los años 70 sin duda han sido la década de la música disco."

podcast.title: Dominant Sound Before "Música Blanca"
podcast.body: In the early 1980s, disco music was a dominant genre in discotheques, often played for dancing and casual entertainment. The emergence of "música blanca" at Barraca, spearheaded by DJs Juan Santamaría and Carlos Simó, marked a conscious effort to differentiate from and move beyond these popular "black sounds." "Porque a las discotecas se solía ir a bailar, pero sobretodo al llegar y hacer el tonto."

podcast.title: Elevation of DJs
podcast.body: Disco music, emerging in the late 1960s and early 1970s, is credited with elevating DJs for the first time, coinciding with the birth of club culture where DJs became central figures. "la música disco, yo creo que fue la música que ralzo a los DJs por primera vez."

podcast.title: Evolution in the 1980s
podcast.body: During the 1980s, disco music evolved into two main branches: its more pop-oriented side developed into New Wave (e.g., Devo) and Synth Pop (e.g., Simple Minds), while its club-oriented side evolved into House Music and, in more elitist circles, Techno, all drawing their foundations from 1970s disco. "durante los años 80 lo que había sido la música disco evolucionados ramas."

podcast.title: Reign in the 1970s
podcast.body: Disco music, alongside club culture, dominated the 1970s, preceding the next major technological shift that would transform DJing. "tras el reinado durante los años 70 de la cultura de glúpila, música disco."

podcast.title: Survival in New York's Gay Communities
podcast.body: Despite the rapid decline of disco after 1978, it did not entirely die out. A small core group, particularly in New York, closely linked to the homosexual and gay communities, kept the music alive, leading to the emergence of acts like Village People. "hubo unos pequeños grupos de la música disco que sí sobrevivieron, bueno los Bonim aguantaron unos años más, pero sobre todo hubo un pequeño núcleo en Nueva York, muy ligado a las comunidades homosexuales, a los comunidades gayes de Nueva York, a que mantuvieron viva la música disco."
